lines.text: Seven pages. I have cut it to six. Progress.
A goose bit me this morning. I have decided to take it as a sign of something.

found.note: He hands you the page he cut. He would rather someone had it.

lines.text: The Lord gives the harvest. The Notch gives me forty minutes to bless it. Less if it turns cold.
Four pages. They were very good about it. Only Thaddeus Rook slept, and he went home first to do it.
There are three pies left, Eldwin, and I am a shepherd to all of them.
I gave thanks for a mild autumn, as I do every year. I have been wondering lately who I ought to be thanking.
Thirty years of "Soldier's Joy". They'd riot if I didn't. I might riot if I do.
Got a new one. No name yet. It goes like wind down a chimney.
Came to me up by the old wall, of all places. You ever hear a tune in a wall, Eldwin?
I've heard a great many things in that wall.
They want "Soldier's Joy" again. I'll give it to them twice, and slip the new one in between while they're catching their breath.
Played the new one last night. Nobody danced. Nobody left, either. They just stood and listened, like it owed them something.
Deacon don't like to be hurried. Neither do I. We get along.
He pulled a stump out of the north road this spring. Nobody asked him to. He just leaned.
Twelve years old. Same as a man of seventy, near enough. Still leans, though.
The Danforth boy follows us about. Deacon stepped on him once. They came to an understanding.
Pulling match is in the morning. I told him. He didn't say anything. That's how you know he heard.
Deacon considers Eldwin for some time. He does not hurry about it, and when he has finished he goes back to chewing.
It's not finished. It needs to be worse.
Crows don't care about scary. Judges do. I'm building for judges.
That's Pa's coat on it. He doesn't know. Now you know. Now we both know.
Mrs. Combs looked at it and went straight home. That's the best anyone's said about it.
Don't laugh. The last one who laughed, I made one of him.
Muffler? It's autumn, ain't it. Autumn's when it starts.
Sit if you like. Bench don't mind. I'm used to it. Well, there's no bench. There was. I've outlasted it.
When I was a boy the frost came down off the mountain like a dog let off its rope. Hasn't done that in a long while. Somebody's been minding it, I expect.
Have they, now.
I'm home by dark, all the same. The night air's got teeth this year.
